title: An interest counts only when named
statement: When scoring whether an item is personalised to a student's interests, count an interest only when the student-facing text names it, and keep that score out of every correctness score.
detail: The AP work's evaluator scores interest relevance as a binary metric: it passes only when at least one listed interest is literally named in the student-facing text, and inferred or thematic connections do not pass (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/evaluators/base.py`). The prompt calls it an engagement measure, not a correctness measure, and tells the judge not to let it influence any other metric. A deterministic literal-mention check in the same file backs the rule.
against: A literal mention can still fail if it is shoehorned in a way that makes the question incoherent or doesn't engage the interest (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/evaluators/base.py`, L1145-1147).

evidence.quote: **Rule:** the content must reference AT LEAST ONE of the listed … interests by literally naming it.
No listed interest is literally named. Inferred … or thematic connections DO NOT pass
This is an engagement/relevance measure, not a correctness … measure.
Do NOT let this metric influence any other metric … (factual_accuracy, educational_accuracy, clarity_precision, … etc.) — those judge correctness, not engagement.
A literal mention can still fail (score 0.0) if it is … shoehorned in a way that makes the question incoherent
